newDescription:
In this Year 3 Maths lesson, pupils develop their understanding of fractions on number lines, including how to label, compare and count with fractions.

This lesson includes:
✔ Revisiting fractions of shapes and recognising equivalent fractions
✔ Drawing and labelling fraction number lines from zero to one whole
✔ Understanding that the denominator shows how many equal intervals the whole is divided into
✔ Recognising that all equal fractional parts together make one whole
✔ Labelling number lines in fifths, quarters, sevenths, ninths and other fractions
✔ Understanding that the numerator increases while the denominator stays the same as we move along a number line
✔ Distinguishing between interval spaces and dividing marks when drawing number lines
✔ Identifying incorrectly labelled fraction number lines
✔ Comparing fractions using aligned number lines
✔ Counting forwards in fractions
✔ Counting backwards in fractions
✔ Solving movement problems on fraction number lines
✔ Finding fractions a given number of steps forwards or backwards
✔ Recognising fractions that are smaller than, equal to or greater than one half

Pupils begin by revisiting familiar fractions before showing them on number lines. They learn to divide the distance from zero to one whole into equal intervals and label each point correctly.

The lesson then develops accuracy with number lines. Pupils identify common mistakes such as counting marks instead of spaces, compare fractions by aligning zero and one on separate number lines, and explain which fraction is closer to one.

Later activities focus on counting forwards and backwards in fractions. Pupils move along number lines in equal fractional steps and solve questions involving starting points, jumps and missing fractions.

The final section uses number lines to compare fractions with one half, helping pupils identify which fractions lie below, exactly at or above one half.

By the end of the lesson, learners will be able to draw and label fraction number lines accurately, compare fractions using their positions, count forwards and backwards in fractions, and recognise fractions relative to one half.
